# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Bank Statement Labeling Codebase Report

## 1. Overall Project Structure

Flask microservice for Indian bank transaction enrichment (categories, payee, sub-tags).

```
/app/
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask/pandas/fuzzywuzzy/scipy deps
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # POST /categorizeTransaction pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # Per-bank category + partyName rules (~35 banks)
        │   ├── HDFC.py, SBI.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py              # clean_input_df, sep_by_*, py_extract, fuzzy_match
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Shared subcategory keyword regexes
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific narration patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Subcategory + merchantType (shared)
            ├── CleanName.py            # Merchant name normalization (~1971 lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Heuristic salary clustering
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer detection
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM rollup categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # PFM display strings
            ├── CardPurpose.py / CardCleanNames.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── Transaction*Enums.py
```

### Pipeline (`Controller.categorizeTransaction`, ~lines 69–150+)

For each bank, order is fixed:

1. **Bank script** → `transactionCategory`, initial `transactionSubcategory`, raw `partyName` / `party2`
2. **CC path** (if credit card): `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`
3. **`purpose()`** → sub-tags (SALARY, LOAN, FUEL, bounce type, …) + merchantType
4. **`clean_names()`** → normalize/canonicalize party names
5. **`internal_payment()`** (if accountHolder present)
6. **`salary_detection()`** (SAVING only)
7. Optional PFM: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`

Default category when nothing matches: **`TRANSFER`**.

---

## 2. Where Each Concern Lives

| Concern | Primary location | Key functions |
|--------|------------------|---------------|
| **Category** | `BankScripts/*.py` | `categorize_*_transactions` — ordered `np.select` on description/remark/type |
| **Payee / counterparty** | Same bank scripts (party extract) + `CleanName.clean_names` | `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract` |
| **Sub-tags** | Bank script (early) + `Purpose.purpose` + `SalaryDetection` + `InternalPayment` | `purpose`, `salary_detection`, `internal_payment` |
| **Cheque detection** | Per-bank CHQ/CLG/remark-number rules | e.g. HDFC 69–75, 100; Axis 54–59; ICICI 69–72 |
| **Salary tagging** | Bank subcategory rules + `Purpose` SALARY regex + `salary_detection` | Purpose 14–16; HDFC 119, 124; Axis 99; ICICI 105, 113 |
| **Transfer direction parsing** | Bank party extract + cleanup | HDFC 256–257; SBI 131–132, 181, 190; ICICI 159, 201–203, 231–232; `TRF_STOP_WORDS` |
| **Slash-delimited refs** | `AppUtil.sep_by_` + bank-specific index picks | Axis 116–151; ICICI 136–183; YES NEFT/UPI |
| **Bounce / reversal** | Bank category rules + Purpose bounce sub-tags | HDFC 25–27, 98–99; ICICI 18, 49–50; Purpose 145–147 |

### Shared helpers

```14:15:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py
def sep_by_(description, n1, n2):
    return description.str.split('/').str[n1:n2].str.join('')
```

Slash fields are taken by **fixed index slices**, not “last non-numeric token”.

---

## 3. Tests

**None found.** No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `*_spec.py`, or README with fixtures. Only a single git commit (`import codebase`). All labeling behavior is untested.

---

## 4. Bug Hypotheses (with code locations)

---

### Bug A — Credit with long all-numeric reference: was cheque deposit, now generic `TRANSFER`

**Hypothesis:** Cheque is only recognized when remark/description matches **narrow numeric or CHQ keyword patterns**. Longer all-numeric refs miss those rules and fall through to default `TRANSFER`.

**Strongest sites:**

| File | Lines | Rule |
|------|-------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` | **100** | Cheque only if `remark` length **exactly 15** and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` | **58–59** | Cheque if remark `^[0-9]{5,6}$` only |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/YES.py` | **52–53** | Remark `^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Kotak.py` | **65–67** | Remark `^[0-9]{3,5}$` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py` | **60–61** | Remark `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| Most banks | end of category block | `default="TRANSFER"` |

HDFC also needs description CHQ/CHEQUE keywords (lines 73–75). A credit whose **only** cheque signal is a long numeric remark/reference (outside the 15-char zero-padded shape) becomes `TRANSFER`.

**Why “used to be cheque”:** Either remark format changed (longer refs / fewer leading zeros), or an older broader rule was never ported into this snapshot. There is **no** general “long all-numeric credit ⇒ cheque” rule.

---

### Bug B — Salary credit with bare numeric narration lost `SALARY` sub-tag

**Hypothesis (primary):** HDFC’s bare-6-digit salary rule never fires because of an **`accountType` typo**.

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", ...) & ... & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

Everywhere else the API uses **`"SAVING"`** (Controller, Purpose, ICICI, Indusind).  
`accountType=="SAVINGS"` is almost certainly always false → bare `123456`-style credits stay untagged.

**Secondary factors:**

1. **`Purpose.purpose` (14–16)** needs description to match `SALARY` / `"salary"` / `SAL_IMPS` — pure digits never match.
2. **`salary_detection` (line 50)** requires `partyName` non-empty for the main candidate set. Bare numeric narrations usually get empty `partyName` (HDFC line 261 blanks non-alpha party names). Scenario 1.3 (lines 90–110) can still tag by amount frequency without partyName, but only when amount mode frequency equals month span — fragile for one-offs.
3. Rule is also limited to **exactly 6 digits** (`^[0-9]{6}$`). 5/7/8+ digit payroll codes never qualify even if SAVINGS were fixed.

---

### Bug C — Narration opens with direction word → counterparty empty/wrong

**Hypothesis:** Direction tokens (`TO`/`FROM`/`TRF TO`/`TRANSFER FROM`/…) are either kept as the “name”, stripped leaving nothing, or extracted with the **wrong capture group**.

**Key sites:**

| File | Lines | Issue |
|------|-------|--------|
| **ICICI.py** | **159** | `py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO\|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` → group **0 is TO/FROM**, not the name (should be `index=1`) |
| **HDFC.py** | **256–257** | Strips only if party already matches `^Trn?f To \|^Paid To \|…`; if bank extract never runs, direction stays or whole field blanks via CLEAN1 |
| **HDFC.py** | **BankRegexConstants 106** | `HDFC_CLEAN1` includes bare `transfer` → **blanks** partyName containing “transfer” |
| **SBI.py** | **131–132** | Extracts after stripping `TRANSFER TO/FROM [0-9]{11}` only for that shape |
| **SBI.py** | **181, 190** | `TRF_STOP_WORDS` / Transfer To\|From cleanup can wipe residual text |
| **ICICI.py** | **201–203, 231–232** | IMPS “ To ” parsing is order-sensitive; wrong branch → empty or truncated |
| **Axis.py** | **167–169** | `^TRANSFER TO ` strip; `^FROM$` / `^TRANSFER$` nulled |
| **BankRegexConstants.py** | **65** | `TRF_STOP_WORDS` includes `^To Transfer.*`, `Transfer From.*`, `^Trf ` |

Classic failure: narration like `TO JOHN DOE` / `TRFR TO:ACME` → extract keeps `To`/`TO` or empties after stop-word wipe; CleanName never recovers a real payee.

---

### Bug D — Bill / slash narration `type/sub-type/numeric-ref/payee` lifts numeric ref instead of final payee

**Hypothesis:** Fixed `sep_by_(desc, i, i+1)` indices target a **middle** slash field (often the numeric ref), not the last alphabetic segment.

**`sep_by_` semantics** (`AppUtil.py` 14–15): take `split('/')[n1:n2]` only.

**High-impact rules:**

| File | Lines | Behavior |
|------|-------|----------|
| **Axis.py** | **146–147** | TRANSFER with 1–2 slashes → **`sep_by_(..., 0, 1)` = first token** (type), never last payee |
| **Axis.py** | **122, 130** | UPI/IMPS/NEFT → indices 3 or 2 (often UTR/ref mid-field) |
| **ICICI.py** | **147–151, 154–158** | `BIL/...`, `INF/NEFT`, NEFT/RTGS use fixed indices 2–5 |
| **ICICI.py** | **175, 179** | `ACH/` → index 1 or 2 (can be numeric mandate id) |
| **ICICI.py** | **206, 233** | If extracted party is pure digits → later blanked (`[0-9]{6,}`) → empty counterparty |
| **ICICI.py** | **160** | `^TRF/` → index 1 only |

Example shape `BIL/ONL/1234567890/ACME CORP`:
- Rules that take index 2 get `1234567890`
- ICICI cleanup **233** then clears pure-numeric party names → empty payee  
There is **no** “prefer last non-numeric slash segment” fallback.

---

### Bug E — Offsetting credit after matching debit labeled bounce, not reversal

**Hypothesis:** Adjacent debit→credit with same amount/description is classified as **`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`**, while **`REVERSAL`** is either missing or gated too tightly (and in HDFC, on the wrong row).

**Critical logic:**

**ICICI** (`ICICI.py` **49–50**):

```49:50:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
# REVERSAL only if narration also matches IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS
# else same adjacent match → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

Any matching reverse of ACH, bill pay, card, internal FT, etc. becomes **bounce**.

**HDFC** (`HDFC.py` **98–99**):

```98:99:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
# REVERSAL: credit after debit, same amount, description == shift(periods=2), AND IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS
# BOUNCE:   credit after debit, same amount, description == shift(periods=1)   ← no channel filter
```

Problems:
1. REVERSAL compares description to **`shift(2)`** (two rows back), not the preceding debit (`shift(1)`). Adjacent true reversals almost never hit REVERSAL.
2. Bounce rule has **no** auto-pay keyword filter — any same-narration refund/reversal looks like bounce.
3. Earlier keyword REVERSAL (line 25) needs “REVERSAL/REV/…” in text; silent offsetting credits won’t match.

**Also:** Standard Chartered **60** only bounce for `NACH DR IW`; Saraswat **20** has REVERSAL for rails only (like ICICI).

Purpose then treats bounce categories specially (clears some sub-tags at 173, merchant types at 294). Users see “bounce” instead of “reversal” on intentional reverse transfers.

---

## 5. Quick Reference — Core Files & Functions

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Orchestration |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/{Bank}.py` | Category + party extract |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` → `purpose()` | Shared sub-tags / merchantType |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` → `clean_names()` | Payee canonicalization |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` → `salary_detection()` | Recurrent salary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self payments |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | `sep_by_*`, `py_extract` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | SALARY, bounce reason regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | CHQ/FT/TRF patterns, `TRF_STOP_WORDS` |

---

## 6. Suggested Fix Directions (for implementers)

| Bug | Likely fix |
|-----|------------|
| **A** | Broaden cheque remark rules (e.g. longer pure-numeric remarks) and/or treat long numeric credits with cheque-like remarks as `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` before default TRANSFER |
| **B** | Change HDFC line 124 `SAVINGS` → `SAVING`; optionally allow other digit lengths; ensure salary_detection path for empty partyName |
| **C** | Fix ICICI line 159 `index=1`; strip leading direction tokens before extract; remove over-broad `transfer` from `HDFC_CLEAN1` or scope it |
| **D** | For slash narrations, prefer **last** segment that looks like a name (has letters, not pure digits), not fixed mid indices |
| **E** | HDFC: REVERSAL use `shift(1)` like ICICI; restrict AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE to auto-pay/ACH patterns; treat non-mandate same-amount reverse credits as REVERSAL |

I did not find any automated tests covering these rules; regressions would only show up via production/forum reports.
</task_result>

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me look more carefully at the cheque rule. The user said "a credit whose reference note is nothing but a long all-numeric string". In HDFC, the remark field is used for cheque detection with exact...The cheque rule is broken because the pattern `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` combined with `len().eq(15)` can never match—11 zeros + 5 digits is 16 characters, not 15. That’s why a plain all-numeric 15-character string (the HDFC remark 0000000000012345) is being treated as a generic transfer instead of a cheque deposit.
